value.name: Migraine
value.description: Migraine is a neurological condition characterized by recurrent, moderate to severe headaches. These headaches are often unilateral and pulsating, and can be accompanied by other symptoms like nausea and sensitivity to light and sound. Migraines can significantly impact a person's daily life and ability to function.
symptoms: Severe, throbbing headache, often on one side of the head
Visual disturbances (aura) before or during the headache
causes: Changes in brainstem activity and its interaction with the trigeminal nerve system
Environmental triggers (e.g., stress, certain foods, hormonal changes)
Changes in brain chemicals, such as serotonin

value.name: Tension-Type Headache
value.description: Tension-type headaches are the most common type of headache, often described as a constant ache or pressure around the head, especially at the temples or back of the head and neck. They are typically mild to moderate in intensity and do not usually interfere with daily activities. While the exact cause is unknown, stress is a common trigger.
symptoms: Sensation of tightness or pressure across the forehead
Tenderness in scalp, neck, and shoulder muscles
Mild sensitivity to light or sound (less common than migraine)
Feeling of a band tightening around the head
causes: Muscle tension in the neck and scalp

value.name: Sinusitis
value.description: Sinusitis, also known as a sinus infection, is an inflammation or swelling of the tissue lining the sinuses. When sinuses become blocked and filled with fluid, germs can grow and cause an infection. This can lead to facial pain and pressure, nasal congestion, and a reduced sense of smell.
symptoms: Reduced sense of smell and taste

value.name: Concussion
value.description: A concussion is a traumatic brain injury (TBI) caused by a bump, blow, or jolt to the head or by a hit to the body that causes the head and brain to move rapidly back and forth. This sudden movement can cause the brain to bounce around or twist in the skull, creating chemical changes in the brain and sometimes stretching and damaging brain cells. Concussions can affect how you think, feel, and act.
symptoms: Headache or a feeling of pressure in the head

value.name: Meningitis
value.description: Meningitis is an inflammation of the membranes (meninges) surrounding the brain and spinal cord. It is most often caused by a viral infection, but can also be caused by bacteria, fungi, or even certain medications. Bacterial meningitis can be life-threatening and requires prompt medical attention.
symptoms: Rash (in some cases, especially with bacterial meningitis)
causes: Viral infections (e.g., enteroviruses, herpes simplex virus)
Bacterial infections (e.g., Streptococcus pneumoniae, Neisseria meningitidis)
